draft.title: Express rights in the Constitution
card: An express right is a right written directly into the Constitution. Australia's Constitution has only a few.
Section 80 gives a right to trial by jury for a Commonwealth indictable offence. An indictable offence is a serious crime.
Other express rights include freedom of religion from Commonwealth laws, and a ban on discrimination against people because of the state they live in.
Because these rights are in the Constitution, the High Court can strike down a Commonwealth law that breaks them.
draft.remember: A few rights are written into the Constitution, so parliament cannot override them.

a.q: What does it mean to say that the right to trial by jury is an express right?
opts: It is written directly into the Constitution
It is found only in laws made by parliament
It is a right the High Court has implied
It applies to every offence in every state
a.why: An express right is stated in the words of the Constitution. An implied right is one the High Court has found from the Constitution's structure, so that option is wrong.
a.clue: Express means stated in the text.

b.q: Parliament passes a law saying a person charged with a serious Commonwealth crime must be tried by a judge alone. What is the likely result if challenged?
opts: The High Court may strike it down for breaching section 80
The law stands, as parliament can override the Constitution
The law stands, because the crime is only a minor offence
The High Court must rewrite the law to allow a jury
b.why: Section 80 requires a jury for Commonwealth indictable offences, so the law may breach it. Parliament cannot override the Constitution, and the High Court strikes laws down rather than rewriting them.
b.clue: Which section protects trial by jury?

a.best: It is written directly into the Constitution

b.best: The High Court may strike it down for breaching section 80

proposal.title: Express rights in the Constitution

Section 80 gives a right to trial by jury for a Commonwealth indictable offence. An indictable offence is a serious crime.

Because these rights are in the Constitution, the High Court can strike down a Commonwealth law that breaks them. It does not rewrite the law.
proposal.remember: A few rights are written into the Constitution, so an ordinary law cannot override them.

a.q: What does it mean to say that the right to trial by jury is an express right?
opts: It is written in the words of the Constitution
It is drawn from the structure of the Constitution
It is set out in a Commonwealth Act of parliament
It was created by a High Court decision in a case
a.why: An express right is stated in the actual words of the Constitution. A right drawn from the Constitution's structure is not written down, so it is not express, even though it also comes from the Constitution.
a.clue: In everyday speech, what does it mean to say something expressly?

b.q: The Commonwealth Parliament passes a law saying people charged with a Commonwealth indictable offence must be tried by a judge alone. If the law is challenged, what would the High Court most likely do?
opts: Strike it down, as it breaches the right to a jury
Uphold it, as parliament can override the Constitution
Uphold it, as the jury right covers only state crimes
Rewrite it, so that a jury hears the trial instead
b.why: Section 80 of the Constitution gives a right to a jury for Commonwealth indictable offences, so the law breaks an express right and can be struck down. Parliament cannot override the Constitution with an ordinary law, and the High Court strikes laws down rather than rewriting them.
b.clue: Can an ordinary law change what the Constitution says?

a.best: It is written in the words of the Constitution

b.best: Strike it down, as it breaches the right to a jury
